turnStructure.description: Each game turn is divided into 32 impulses. All players resolve movement simultaneously on each impulse based on their ship's speed.

specialImpulses.impulse1: No units move (starships restricted to speed 31 or less). Speed-32 seeking weapons one hex from targets hit automatically.
specialImpulses.impulse32: All units move, including the slowest. Targets at range limit of overloaded torpedoes (8 hexes) cannot escape.

sequenceOfPlay.name: Energy Allocation
sequenceOfPlay.description: Each player fills out an Energy Allocation form, spending energy on movement, shields, weapons, and special systems for the upcoming turn.

sequenceOfPlay.name: Self-Destruction
sequenceOfPlay.description: Crippled ships may choose to self-destruct, creating a sizable explosion that can damage nearby ships.

sequenceOfPlay.name: Sensor Lock-On
sequenceOfPlay.description: Players use sensors to lock onto enemy targets for weapons fire.

sequenceOfPlay.name: Initial Activity
sequenceOfPlay.description: Preliminary actions before movement and combat, such as launching shuttles or probes.

sequenceOfPlay.name: Impulse Procedure
sequenceOfPlay.description: The main combat loop repeated for each of the 32 impulses: movement, weapons fire, seeking weapon resolution, and damage allocation.

impulseProcedure.description: Ships move according to their speed on the Movement Chart. Speed determines which impulses a ship moves on.
Phasers, disruptors, and photon torpedoes fire. Hit probability and damage depend on range bands.
Plasma torpedoes and drones move toward targets. Interception attempts are resolved.
Tractor beams can be activated or released. Used to tow ships or hold seeking weapons.
Damage from weapons fire is applied to shields first, then to internal systems via the Damage Allocation Chart.

mapSystem.facing: Each ship maintains a definite heading on the hex grid, changeable by 60 degrees or less per turn under normal rules.

ruleReferenceSystem.example: D6.683 — Third subsection of D6.68 (Disrupted Fire Control), under D6.6 (Active Fire Control), in chapter D (Combat)
